moat_against: Commodity price-taker: fat, protein and renewable diesel prices are set by markets, not by Darling
DGD earnings are policy-dependent (RIN values, LCFS, 45Z production credits, small-refinery exemptions)
ROIC proxy fell 15.1% -> 2.5% over FY2022 to latest FY — returns through the recent cycle do not support a wide moat
Leverage: net debt $3,848,789,000 = 8.0x normalized owner's earnings
Acquisition-built growth (Valley Proteins, Gelnex, FASA) carries goodwill/integration risk
moat_for: Largest global renderer — ~15% of world animal by-products, 260+ facilities; collection route density and plant permitting are hard to replicate
Integrated captive feedstock (animal fats, used cooking oil) makes Diamond Green Diesel a structurally low-cost renewable diesel producer
Collagen/gelatin scale (Rousselot, Gelnex) — roughly 30% of global collagen supply, growing food/health demand
Flexibility to route fats between feed, food and fuel markets captures value across cycles
moat_justification: Scale and route-density moat in rendering (world's largest renderer, ~15% of world animal by-products, integrated low-carbon feedstock supply into Diamond Green Diesel, leading collagen position via Rousselot/Gelnex), but the economics are commodity-priced and policy-levered: gross margin is stable ~22-26% yet the roic_proxy fell from 15.1% (FY2022) to 12.2%, 9.8%, 4.4% and 2.5% (latest FY) as DGD earnings swung with RIN/LCFS/45Z policy, and net debt is 8.0x normalized OE. A 5 = moderate/narrow: real collection-network barriers, no pricing power over fat/protein/diesel prices.
name: Darling Ingredients Inc.
one_liner: Real but narrow moat (5/10) in a commodity/policy-levered business — does not clear 15% at $60.52: weighted IRR 9.21% on the normalized base, IV@15% $31.34; it would clear 15% only at or below ~$31 (latest-FY-base method tops out at Tier C, 11.51%).
